# This repo is build output. Do not edit it by hand.

Every `.html` file here is generated by `scripts/build-site.mjs` and
`scripts/build-certificates.mjs` in **`sbdavidjlemmons-hub/honest-travel-group`**.
That repo is the source. This one is what GitHub Pages serves.

**A hand-edit here works right up until it doesn't.** The change goes live, the
deploy is green, and then the next generator run overwrites it with no error and
no warning. That has happened three times:

- **2026-08-16** (`979a25e`, this repo) — a hand-edit to `thank-you.html` was
  silently reverted by the next build.
- **2026-08-15** (`d7bf40d`, this repo) — `index.html` reverted on rebuild,
  proving the edit did not come from source.
- **2026-08-30** — the visit beacon was hand-added to 44 files here. It worked,
  it was live, and it was one build away from disappearing. It now lives in the
  generator with a build assertion behind it.

## If you need to change a page

Work in `honest-travel-group`: edit the generator, run it, run
`node scripts/check-site.mjs`, diff the regenerated `site/` against this repo,
then bring the output across on a branch and open a PR.

## What legitimately lives here and nowhere else

| Path | Note |
|---|---|
| `CNAME`, `.nojekyll`, `_redirects` | Deployment config. Also emitted by the generator. |
| `js/visit.js`, `js/scoring.js` | Copied in by the build from `scripts/assets/js/`. Edit them **there**. |

## Still a hand-edit, and still at risk

`thank-you.html` carries the partner hand-off — `handoff()`, `ptoken()`, the
`partner.html` link and the local `.ics`, roughly 143 lines — and `partner.html`
has no generator at all. **Neither is reproducible from source yet.** The next
full build takes both. Porting them into `build-site.mjs` is outstanding work,
not a decision that was made.

## Before you merge anything here

Diff the merged tree against what is deployed. A clean auto-merge is not evidence
of a correct one: on 2026-08-30 two sessions independently added the same three
tracking scripts to the 40 certificate pages, git took both sides without a
conflict, and every page was set to fire GA4, Meta and DataMoon twice — inflating
exactly the traffic numbers the intent ranking is read off.
